question: A previously healthy 5-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department because of fever, irritability, malaise, and left knee pain for 4 days. Four days ago, he fell off his bike and scraped his elbow. His temperature is 39.1°C (102.4°F). The patient walks with a limp. Examination shows swelling and point tenderness over the medial aspect of the left knee. An MRI of the left knee shows edema of the bone marrow and destruction of the medial metaphysis of the tibia. Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Fall and scrape" -> "skin breach" -> "bacterial entry" -> "Staphylococcus aureus colonization" -> "bone infection" -> "osteomyelitis" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Fall and scrape" -> "skin breach" -> "bacterial entry" -> "Staphylococcus epidermidis colonization" -> "bone infection" -> "osteomyelitis" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Fall and scrape" -> "skin breach" -> "bacterial entry" -> "Pseudomonas aeruginosa colonization" -> "bone infection" -> "osteomyelitis" -> 50%
CHAIN: "Fall and scrape" -> "skin breach" -> "bacterial entry" -> "Pasteurella multocida colonization" -> "bone infection" -> "osteomyelitis" -> 40%
CHAIN: "Fall and scrape" -> "skin breach" -> "bacterial entry" -> "Brucella melitensis colonization" -> "bone infection" -> "osteomyelitis" -> 30%
analysis: The clinical presentation is suggestive of osteomyelitis, a bone infection that commonly occurs in children. The history of a recent fall and skin abrasion could have provided an entry point for bacteria. Staphylococcus aureus is the most common cause of osteomyelitis in children, especially following trauma or skin injury. The MRI findings of bone marrow edema and metaphyseal destruction are consistent with this diagnosis.
